questions.title: Customers above average paid spend
questions.summary: Return customer_id and revenue for customers whose paid total exceeds the average of paid totals among customers with at least one paid order.
concept: Average customer totals, not order amounts.
questions.task: Return customer_id and revenue for customers whose paid total exceeds the average of paid totals among customers with at least one paid order. Sort by customer_id.
requirements: Average customer totals, not order amounts.
Do not silently include zero-spend customers.
questions.solution:
WITH totals AS (
 SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS revenue
 FROM orders WHERE status='paid' GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT customer_id,revenue FROM totals
WHERE revenue > (SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM totals)
ORDER BY customer_id;
questions.explanation: Compute the average at the customer-total grain, not the raw order grain. Customers without paid orders are excluded from this specifically defined average.
hints: Filter paid orders before grouping.

questions.title: Revenue and event count in PySpark
questions.summary: Build result with customer_id, revenue and event_count from events.
questions.task: Build result with customer_id, revenue and event_count from events. Use built-in aggregations; count rows even when amount is null.
questions.starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

result = (events
    .groupBy("customer_id")
    # Add named aggregates
)
questions.solution:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
result = (events.groupBy("customer_id")
 .agg(F.sum("amount").alias("revenue"),
      F.count("*").alias("event_count")))
questions.explanation: groupBy causes an aggregation shuffle unless compatible partitioning already satisfies the plan. count("*") counts rows; count("amount") excludes null amounts. This is review, never browser Spark execution.
